# Lab 12.7: K-means Clustering

## What We Are Going to Do
Segment customers by recency, frequency and spend with k-means, and read the cluster centres.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Build RFM features.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab12.customer_rfm AS
SELECT
  user_id,
  DATE_DIFF(CURRENT_DATE(), DATE(MAX(created_at)), DAY) AS recency_days,
  COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS frequency,
  ROUND(SUM(sale_price), 2) AS monetary
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items`
WHERE status = 'Complete'
GROUP BY user_id;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Train k-means with 4 clusters.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE MODEL lab12.customer_segments
OPTIONS (model_type = 'KMEANS', num_clusters = 4, standardize_features = TRUE, kmeans_init_method = 'KMEANS++')
AS SELECT recency_days, frequency, monetary FROM lab12.customer_rfm;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Read the centroids.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT centroid_id, feature, ROUND(numerical_value, 1) AS value
FROM ML.CENTROIDS(MODEL lab12.customer_segments)
ORDER BY centroid_id, feature;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Name each cluster from its centre, for example "recent big spenders" or "lost customers".

4. **[SQL] Assign every customer.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT centroid_id, COUNT(*) AS customers, ROUND(AVG(monetary), 2) AS avg_spend
FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL lab12.customer_segments, (SELECT * FROM lab12.customer_rfm))
GROUP BY centroid_id ORDER BY centroid_id;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[Console] Compare values of k.** In the model's **Evaluation** tab, read the **Davies-Bouldin index**. Train again with `num_clusters = 3` and `5`. A lower index means better-separated clusters.

6. **[CLI] Count customers per segment from bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
'SELECT centroid_id, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM ML.PREDICT(MODEL lab12.customer_segments, (SELECT * FROM lab12.customer_rfm)) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Features | Recency, frequency, monetary |
| Standardisation | Puts features on the same scale |
| Centroids | Describe each segment |
| Choosing k | Lower Davies-Bouldin is better |
